look_here_first: Look for a VERY LOW rhizomatous muhly: numerous extremely fine, inward-rolled threadlike leaves, slender usually 20–40 cm culms and a short narrow flowering head, sometimes partly held inside the top leaf sheath. True creeping SCALY underground rhizomes distinguish it from surface-stolon nimblewill, but rhizomes must be exposed for confirmation.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hagenbuch & Lemke's Texas Hill Country grass specimen appendix documents Muhlenbergia utilis from Bandera, Blanco, Gillespie, Kerr, Llano, and Travis counties, all inside the project target zone.

best_field_traits: very narrow filiform involute leaf blades
small narrow panicle, sometimes partly included in upper sheath
often in moist depressions, stream margins, or seep-like grassland microsites
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Unlike the large bunch-forming M. lindheimeri or M. ×involuta, M. utilis is a much shorter rhizomatous grass with threadlike leaves and a small narrow inflorescence.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole low patch from the side with flowering culms in context.
Gently exposed underground scaly rhizome with leaves/stems attached and mm ruler; backfill after photograph.
Fresh rolled threadlike leaf blade cross-section + a very short membranous ligule.
Entire small inflorescence showing whether partly enclosed by the upper leaf sheath.
crew_field_check: Spot the very fine grass foliage and low growth in the original whole-patch photograph; do not mistake dry dead leaves for evidence of rhizomes.
In the closer image, trace true slender grass blades with the fingers for scale. The tiny leaf width can be seen, but their inward-rolled edges cannot be measured here.
Confirm with an exposed SCALY UNDERGROUND rhizome and ligule; distinguish nimblewill's visible surface runners from true below-ground rhizomes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: M. schreberi spreads by ABOVE-GROUND slender stolons which root at nodes, usually with short flattened leaf blades; M. utilis has underground scaly rhizomes and very fine involute blades. M. reverchonii forms a tight compact upright tuft with an open flowering panicle. Sporobolus may look similar but its spikelet structures differ on mature dissection.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Aparejo grass / Aparejo muhly — look here first
steps: Image 1 is the wide plant patch beside a sidewalk and shoes; start here for habit and general scale only.
Image 2 is the finger close-up of threadlike living leaves and stems. The finger is not a millimeter ruler, and leaf cross-sections are still hidden.
Image 3 is a DIFFERENT grass, nimblewill: compare its short sideways blades along distinct above-ground joints.
Confirm an attached SCALY BELOW-GROUND rhizome of aparejo versus true above-ground rooting stolons in nimblewill; photograph both with a mm scale. Neither diagnostic is visible in current images.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use the photographed growth-form details only to choose a candidate. Confirm with the missing rooting/rhizome/ligule reproductive details.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Photographed stems, leaves and patch do not establish a rooted node, a subterranean rhizome or a microscopic ligule.
